about: Host-side precedence vectors for tools/related_claims_check.py (x402-foundation/tsc#4, 2026-09-24). Verdict order FAIL > CANNOT_ESTABLISH > PASS: an adverse finding always wins, an absence never hides one. Exit codes: 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 CANNOT_ESTABLISH (this checker's convention; the charter picks the number).
boundary: A referenced proof the relying party does not hold is CANNOT_ESTABLISH (absence), not FAIL: it is third-party data, and failing would assert something unchecked about the artifact. The checker is stdlib-only (pure-Python BIP-340), so the 'host lacks a crypto backend' absence cannot arise here.

vectors.why: outer signature forged (adverse, needs no missing input) + inner proof not supplied (absence): FAIL must win
every check that can run passes; the comparison cannot be recomputed without the inner proof
inner proof invalid and recomputed comparison contradicts the recorded result
same inputs as absence_only, but the caller declared its referenced set complete: a missing proof is a policy refusal
the flag changes nothing when the referenced proof is present and valid
